Definition: from G1537 and the base of G5157; to deflect, i.e. turn away (literally or figuratively):--avoid, turn (aside, out of the way).
BiblicalUsage: ektrépō means to turn aside. In 1 Timothy 1:6, the text says "From which some having swerved have turned aside unto vain jangling." In 1 Timothy 5:15, the text says "For some are already turned aside after Satan."
TheologicalSignificance: What ektrépō teaches me is that repentance is not grovelling; it is turning around and walking the other way. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
